properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Glacier Bay; Eastern Chichagof Island; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 7:59PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The second round of heavy rain is expected to bring an additional
0.5 to 1.5 inches tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end
QPF amounts expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More
localized lower or higher amounts are possible due to terrain
effects.

Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central
panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 10:49PM CDT until October 17 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 10:27PM CDT until October 16 at 1:30AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Val Verde County in south central Texas...

* Until 130 AM CDT.

* At 1027 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pafford Crossing and Devils River State Nat Area Big Satan.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
